title: When The Present Eats The Future | NOEMA
gist: Nathan Gardels argues consumer democracies are structurally short-termist ('the present eats the future') while China's market-state planning has won green tech, citing ~70% EV share of China's new car sales and ~80% of world batteries, and proposes quotas-then-tariffs rather than bans on Chinese green imports.

insights.claim: Consumer democracies lack a constituency for the future because political, cultural and market feedback signals all reward short-term gratification, from fast fashion to elections to quarterly earnings.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Systemic bias against long-horizon investment is a structural headwind for Western infrastructure and industrial policy.
insights.quote: The Achilles heel of consumer democracies is that there is precious little constituency for the future in the present.

insights.claim: Democratic transfer of power can fully reverse policies most voters endorsed only four years earlier, so sticking to a course long enough to bear fruit is not a reliable feature of the system.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Policy-reversal risk should be priced into long-gestation sectors dependent on subsidies or regulation.

insights.claim: Market economies roundly frown on dirigiste industrial policy, but the opposite rigidity of the consumerist short-term mentality is a less-appreciated governance failure.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Reframes industrial policy debate: absence of it is also a choice with costs.

insights.claim: China combines a long-term planning framework checked by market signals and strategic subsidies, with a 'whole dragon' approach aligning start-up subsidies, sourcing, supply chains and production capacity vertically once the Party ordains a goal.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Vertical alignment explains rapid scale-up in targeted sectors; expect the same playbook in the next strategic industry.

insights.claim: The flip side of China's model is overproduction spilling into world markets, threatening jobs and industry elsewhere, and its consensus stability depends on repressive control.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Expect continued export pressure and trade friction in sectors China targets.

insights.claim: The US leader dominates the 24-hour news cycle via social media barrages while China's leader has charted a roadmap for the next half century.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Contrast of planning horizons underlies the author's strategic-competition view.

insights.claim: Nearly 70% of new car sales in China are EVs, half of global EV sales are Chinese-made, China produces around 80% of the world's batteries, holds 70% of battery patents and half of the world's large-scale battery storage capacity.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Western battery and EV supply chains remain structurally dependent on China.
insights.locator: China's Long March To Owning Green Technologies

insights.claim: In 2012 a Chinese diplomat laid out China's decisive shift to EVs and battery storage R&D to doubtful listeners, when China was not in the auto race and the Chevy Volt was the world's most produced EV; the plan was executed over 14 years.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Stated Chinese long-term plans have historically been delivered; take current ones seriously.
insights.locator: China's Long March To Owning Green Technologies

insights.claim: China required developers to build or commission large-scale storage as a condition for approving new wind or solar installations, and built out nationwide rapid-charging infrastructure to boost EV use.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Policy linking storage to renewable approvals is a template for grid-scale storage demand.
insights.locator: China's Long March To Owning Green Technologies

insights.claim: California's large battery storage grew from 700 MW in 2019 to 21,000 MW in 2026 with a 52,000 MW goal by 2045, solar met 51% of its demand in May 2026, and about 90% of cells and core components in installed batteries come from China.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Even the leading US storage market is deeply China-dependent, an exposure to tariff and geopolitical risk.
insights.locator: China's Long March To Owning Green Technologies

insights.claim: Rather than banning Chinese green imports, Gardels proposes a reasonable quota beyond which tariffs kick in, limiting damage while letting foreign competition spark domestic scale-up.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Points to quota-plus-tariff designs as a plausible policy form for green-tech trade.

insights.claim: California's fuel-efficiency and clean-energy standards created the market that made Tesla possible, showing regulation can create rather than destroy markets.
insights.speaker: NATHAN GARDELS
insights.so_what: Demand-side regulation is a driver of new-industry formation.
